mainTopic: How בן בתירא views a פסח slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth, when an offering counts as 'too early', and whether living animals can be pushed off forever.
overview: The גמרא is discussing בן בתירא's view of a פסח slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth of ניסן. First it tries reading בן בתירא as holding that ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ allows the whole day. It defends that reading: the ״בָּעָרֶב״ in the פסח verse only teaches that the פסח comes after the afternoon תמיד, just as מנחה is prayed before a late מוסף. But two challenges knock this reading down. The words ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ by the קטורת and the נרות would be extra, and רבי describes the fourteenth as only 'partly' fit. So רבי יוחנן explains that בן בתירא disqualifies a morning slaughter either way. רבי אבהו asks how a valid פסח could then ever exist. Three answers follow: an animal set aside after midday (רבי אבהו), even in the morning (אביי), or even the night before (רב פפא), with support from מעשר בהמה and רבי אפטוריקי. Finally, רבי זירא asks whether רבי יוחנן holds that living animals can be pushed off forever. רבי אבהו proves that he does from the case of a partners' animal, and the גמרא begins drawing three lessons from it, which continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The incense is in the afternoon because it is linked to the lamps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation: the afternoon קטורת must be offered in the afternoon because the תורה links it to the lighting of the נרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: …because it is juxtaposed with the lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer it started just before this point. The afternoon קטורת cannot be offered all day, because the תורה places it next to the lighting of the נרות, which happens in the evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בן בתירא, ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ alone could mean any time of day. The קטורת is different because of a הֶקֵּשׁ: it is set right beside the lamp lighting, and that lighting is clearly an evening act. So the קטורת is pulled into the afternoon too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is compared or linked by being placed next to something in the פסוק (a הֶקֵּשׁ)
The lamps of the מנורה, which are lit in the evening
The incense offered on the inner altar morning and afternoon

phrases.english: as it is juxtaposed with the lamps.
phrases.notes: This refers to שמות 30:8, where burning the incense and lighting the lamps appear in the same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that began just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The case is set apart by a הֶקֵּשׁ that ties the incense to an evening activity.
steps.terutzMaskana: For בן בתירא, the קטורת stays in the afternoon only because it is linked to the נרות.

steps.title: The Passover verse also says 'in the evening'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the פסח also has a clear evening reference, ״בָּעָרֶב״, so how can בן בתירא allow it in the morning?
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is written: "There you shall sacrifice the Passover offering in the evening"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בן בתירא. If an evening reference keeps the קטורת in the afternoon, then the פסח should also be limited, since its own פסוק says ״בָּעָרֶב״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step showed that a clear link to evening overrides the wide reading of ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״. Here the evening reference is in the פסח's own verse, which is even stronger than a הֶקֵּשׁ. So it seems the פסח should not be valid in the morning.

keyTerms.meaning: There too, the same reasoning applies to the other case
In the evening
The Passover offering, slaughtered on the fourteenth of ניסן

phrases.english: There too, it is written:
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the פסח, which בן בתירא allows in the morning.

phrases.english: "There you shall sacrifice the Passover offering
in the evening"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of step 1 against בן בתירא's ruling on the פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן בתירא's ruling that a פסח slaughtered in the morning is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a link to evening keeps the incense in the afternoon, an explicit ״בָּעָרֶב״ in the פסח verse should keep the פסח in the afternoon too.

steps.title: 'In the evening' teaches the order of offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word ״בָּעָרֶב״ in the פסח verse is not about timing. It teaches that one offering must come after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse comes for the rule of "an item should be delayed."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The extra word ״בָּעָרֶב״ is used for a different rule, so it does not limit the פסח to the afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word ״בָּעָרֶב״ is already used for another teaching, it cannot also serve as a time limit for בן בתירא. The rule it teaches is called ״יְאוּחַר דָּבָר״, which means one offering is pushed later than another. The next step shows where this rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: That verse comes for a different purpose
An item should be delayed, meaning offered after another item

phrases.english: That verse is for "an item should be delayed"
that it comes,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is used for a different teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״בָּעָרֶב״ limits the time of the פסח to the afternoon.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בָּעָרֶב״ teaches the order of the פסח and the תמיד, not a time limit.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves the order rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the פסח, which has both ״בָּעָרֶב״ and ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״, comes after the afternoon תמיד, which has only ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: An item about which both "in the evening" and "between the evenings" are said should come after an item about which only "between the evenings" is said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the word ״בָּעָרֶב״ really is used for the order rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח has two time words, ״בָּעָרֶב״ and ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״. The afternoon תמיד has only ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״. The added word ״בָּעָרֶב״ shows the פסח is "later", so it is offered after the תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally "between the evenings"; the afternoon period
The daily offering brought every morning and afternoon

steps.whatToRemember: The ״בָּעָרֶב״ in the פסח verse is used to teach that the פסח comes after the afternoon תמיד. Because of that, it does not stop בן בתירא from allowing the פסח in the morning.
steps.confusionAlert: The ״דָּבָר״ (item) mentioned first is the פסח, and the second ״דָּבָר״ is the afternoon תמיד. The פסח is the one that gets delayed.

phrases.english: As it is taught: an item should be delayed
about which "in the evening" is said
phrases.notes: This is the פסח: ״בָּעָרֶב״ is in דברים 16:6 and ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ is in שמות 12:6.

phrases.english: and "between the evenings,"
after an item about which is said
only "between the evenings."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That ״בָּעָרֶב״ in the פסח verse is used for the rule ״יְאוּחַר דָּבָר״.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the order of the פסח and the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: Can the morning be its time while the afternoon requires delay?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions how this fits together. Is there any offering whose proper time includes the morning, yet in the afternoon it must wait until after the תמיד?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there anything where, if one slaughters it in the morning, you say it is its time, and when the afternoon comes you say "the item should be delayed"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the picture it has built for בן בתירא. It finds it strange that the פסח would be fine in the morning, before the תמיד, but in the afternoon it would have to wait until after the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסח must come after the afternoon תמיד, that suggests it truly belongs late in the day. Yet בן בתירא allows it in the morning, even before the תמיד. The גמרא asks whether any such pattern exists anywhere else. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: But is there anything like this? (a challenging question)
From the morning
Its proper time
When it arrives (when the time comes)

phrases.english: But is there anything
where, if one slaughters it from the morning,
you say it is its time,
but when the afternoon arrives,
you say "the item should be delayed"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the order rule from steps 3-4 fits with בן בתירא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: Combining בן בתירא's morning validity with the rule that the פסח comes after the afternoon תמיד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסח's time includes the morning, it should not have to be pushed after the afternoon תמיד. Having both rules seems inconsistent.

steps.title: Yes: מנחה comes before מוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes. There is such a case: someone who has not yet prayed מוסף by afternoon prays מנחה first, as רבי יוחנן rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה is that one prays מנחה first, and afterward prays מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5 by pointing to a known case that works the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוסף may be prayed in the morning too, yet once it is afternoon, מנחה goes first. In the same way, the פסח could be fit from the morning and still have to wait for the afternoon תמיד. So the picture of the פסח that בן בתירא's view needs is not strange at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The afternoon prayer, which matches the afternoon תמיד
The additional prayer of שבת, ראש חודש, or יום טוב
The practical ruling

phrases.english: Yes;
as Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha is: one prays the afternoon prayer,
and afterward he prays the additional prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 with a parallel case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No item could be valid in the morning and still need to wait for the תמיד in the afternoon.
steps.terutzMaskana: מוסף is exactly such a case: it may be prayed all day, but in the afternoon מנחה comes first.

steps.title: Why the words are needed for the incense and the lamps
steps.stepSummary: If ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ means the whole day, why does the תורה write it for the קטורת and the נרות?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the words ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ written about the קטורת and the נרות, why do I need them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that, for בן בתירא, ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ means the whole day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed that the afternoon קטורת is timed by its link to the lighting of the נרות. The קטורת and the נרות are clearly not done all day. So if ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ just means 'the whole day', the words seem to add nothing there.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense burned in the בית המקדש
The lamps of the מנורה
'Why do I need it?', meaning the words seem extra

phrases.english: And "bein ha'arbayim"
that is written regarding the incense and the lamps,
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּ״בֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ דִּכְתִיב גַּבֵּי קְטֹרֶת וְנֵרוֹת, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the parallel case, the גמרא now attacks the basic reading of ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ as 'all day'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ as 'the whole day' in בן בתירא's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קטורת and the נרות are only done in the afternoon. If the phrase means 'all day', it is pointless in their verse.

steps.title: רבי's answer to רבי יהושע for בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second challenge. It quotes רבי, who answered רבי יהושע for בן בתירא by contrasting the thirteenth, when no part of the day is fit, with the fourteenth, when part of it is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: רבי answered רבי יהושע on behalf of בן בתירא. 'No! You said this about the thirteenth, when no part of the day is fit. Will you say the same about the fourteenth, when part of it is fit?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second challenge by quoting a source. The point of the attack comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע compared a פסח slaughtered for the wrong purpose on the morning of the fourteenth to one slaughtered on the thirteenth. רבי rejected this comparison for בן בתירא. On the fourteenth, he said, 'part' of the day is fit for the פסח, so the morning is treated differently. Notice the exact word 'part'; the גמרא will build on it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In place of', here meaning answering on behalf of someone
Part of the day is fit
The thirteenth of ניסן
The fourteenth of ניסן, the day the פסח is brought

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי – תַּחַת בֶּן בְּתִירָא –
phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi responded, in place of ben Beteira,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, answering on בן בתירא's side.

phrases.english: to the words of Rabbi Yehoshua:
No; if you said this about the thirteenth,
where no part of it is fit,
shall you say it about the fourteenth,
where part of it is fit?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי – תַּחַת בֶּן בְּתִירָא – לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge ('ועוד') to the first one in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of בן בתירא as holding that the פסח is fit all day on the fourteenth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source that speaks for בן בתירא describes the fourteenth as only partly fit.

steps.title: If so, the whole day should be fit
steps.stepSummary: If בן בתירא holds the פסח may be brought all day, then the whole fourteenth is fit, not just part of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, then all of the day is fit!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the point of the challenge set up in step 8. The words 'part of it is fit' do not match a view that the whole day is fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our reading said that for בן בתירא, ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ covers the whole day. In that case רבי should have said 'all of it is fit', not 'part of it'. So רבי's wording suggests that even בן בתירא sees only the afternoon as the proper time.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if it is so', introducing what would follow from the claim
All of it is fit

steps.whatToRemember: There are two challenges to reading בן בתירא as 'the whole day': (1) the words ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ by the קטורת and the נרות would be extra, and (2) רבי speaks of the fourteenth as only 'partly' fit.

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if בן בתירא really holds the פסח may be brought all day.

phrases.english: all of it is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 8 set up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that for בן בתירא the פסח is fit for the whole fourteenth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי said 'part of it is fit'. If the whole day were fit, he would have said 'all of it'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's New Explanation of בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that בן בתירא disqualifies a פסח slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth, whether for its sake or not, because part of that day is fit for the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: בן בתירא would disqualify a פסח slaughtered on the fourteenth in the morning, whether for its own sake or not for its own sake, since part of that day is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier explanation of בן בתירא was knocked down by the challenges in steps 7-9, so the גמרא brings a brand-new explanation from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanation said that for בן בתירא, the whole day is fit for the פסח. רבי יוחנן reverses this: the morning is not the time to bring the פסח, but because the afternoon of the fourteenth is fit, the whole day already counts as the פסח's day. So slaughtering it in the morning is invalid either way: for its own sake it is too early, and slaughtering it for a different purpose on its own day does not save it.

keyTerms.meaning: disqualifies, rules invalid
in the morning
for its own sake (as a פסח) / not for its own sake (as some other offering)
part of it is fit, meaning part of the day is fit for the פסח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two explanations. Before this step, בן בתירא was understood to say the whole day is fit. רבי יוחנן says the morning is NOT fit, and only the fact that the afternoon is fit makes the whole day count as the פסח's day.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
Ben Beteira would disqualify
a Pesach offering that one slaughtered
on the fourteenth, in the morning,
whether for its own sake or not for its own sake,
since part of it is fit.
phrases.notes: "Part of it" means part of the day: the afternoon of the fourteenth is the proper time for the פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation of בן בתירא that the challenges in steps 7-9 undermined.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New interpretation of the disputed opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בן בתירא holds that the whole fourteenth is fit for the פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: בן בתירא disqualifies a morning slaughter either way, because the day partly belongs to the פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth is invalid according to בן בתירא, whether for its sake or not.

steps.title: רבי אבהו Asks How a Valid פסח Is Ever Possible
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו mocks רבי יוחנן's explanation: if the morning disqualifies the animal, a valid פסח could never exist, whether it was set aside that day or the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו scoffed at this: If so, how could you ever find a valid פסח according to בן בתירא? If he set it aside today, it is rejected from the start. If he set it aside yesterday, it was fit and then rejected!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו attacks רבי יוחנן's explanation by showing that it leads to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal cannot be validly offered on the morning of the fourteenth, then an animal set aside that morning starts out unusable. An animal set aside the day before was usable then, but it becomes unusable in the morning, and once an offering is pushed off it cannot become fit again. Either way, no valid פסח seems possible.

keyTerms.meaning: scoffs at, mocks (literally 'waves his hand at')
he set it aside, designated it as an offering
rejected from the start; unusable from the moment it became an offering
fit and then rejected; once an offering is pushed off, it stays disqualified

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu scoffed at it:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, פֶּסַח כָּשֵׁר לְבֶן בְּתִירָא
phrases.english: If so, a valid Pesach offering according to Ben Beteira,
how can you find it?
If he set it aside now,
phrases.notes: "Now" means the morning of the fourteenth.

phrases.english: it is rejected from the start,
and if he set it aside yesterday,
it was fit and then rejected!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's explanation by drawing out what follows from it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that בן בתירא disqualifies a morning slaughter on the fourteenth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the morning is an unfit time, every פסח is disqualified: one set aside that morning is דחוי מעיקרו, and one set aside earlier is נראה ונדחה. So a valid פסח could never exist.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: A פסח Set Aside After Midday
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו himself answers that a valid פסח is possible when it is set aside after midday on the fourteenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבהו said: Let it be a פסח set aside after midday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers his own question by pointing to a case where a valid פסח is possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After midday the time for the פסח has already arrived. An animal set aside then is never in an unfit state, so it is neither rejected from the start nor fit and then rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: after midday, when the time for slaughtering the פסח begins

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Abbahu said:
Let it be after midday.
phrases.notes: He means the animal is set aside as a פסח after midday on the fourteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by finding a case that avoids both problems.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a specific case where the law can work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No valid פסח is possible under רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: A פסח set aside after midday was never unfit, so it is valid.

steps.title: אביי: Even One Set Aside in the Morning Works
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that even a פסח set aside in the morning is not disqualified, because an offering whose time comes later the same day is not considered 'too early.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say it was set aside in the morning, because an offering is not considered 'lacking time' when its time comes that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different and broader answer to רבי אבהו's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's challenge assumed that an animal set aside in the morning is rejected from the start because its time has not yet come. אביי rejects that assumption: if its time arrives later that day, it does not count as 'too early' at all. So even a morning designation produces a valid פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: from the morning
an offering whose time has not yet arrived
for that same day; its time will arrive later today

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says בן בתירא disqualifies a morning slaughter on the fourteenth. רבי אבהו asks how a valid פסח could ever exist. He answers: one set aside after midday. אביי answers: even one set aside in the morning, since an offering whose time comes that same day is not 'too early.'
steps.whyThisMatters: אביי's rule, that an offering whose time comes that same day is not considered 'too early', is a general principle that applies beyond this case.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You can even say from the morning,
phrases.notes: He means even an animal set aside as a פסח on the morning of the fourteenth.

phrases.english: there is no 'lacking time' for something whose time comes that same day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a broader answer than רבי אבהו's to the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption behind the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An animal set aside on the morning of the fourteenth is rejected from the start because its time has not yet come.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since its time arrives that same day, it is not considered lacking time, so it can be a valid פסח.

steps.title: רב פפא: Even the night before is not too early
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that even a פסח set aside on the night before the fourteenth is not disqualified, because night does not make an animal 'too early.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: You can even say the animal was set aside the night before. Night does not count as 'too early.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives another answer to רבי אבהו's challenge, going even further than אביי. He says a פסח set aside the night before the fourteenth is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי only said that setting it aside on the morning of the fourteenth itself is fine. רב פפא says the night before is also fine, because a night followed by the day the animal can be offered is not called מחוסר זמן. This widens the window of a valid פסח even more.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering whose time has not yet come, so it is 'too early'
From the night before (Aramaic)
You may even say

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
You may even say it was set aside from the night before;
night is not considered 'too early.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא מֵאוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one step further than אביי's answer in step 13: not only the morning, but even the previous night is fine.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Expanding the rule: night before the fit day is not מחוסר זמן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסח set aside before the fourteenth would be 'too early' and disqualified.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even one set aside the night before the fourteenth is valid, since night is not considered מחוסר זמן.

steps.title: Proof from tithing an animal on the night before its eighth day
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that an animal may enter the pen to be tithed on the night before its eighth day, showing night is not 'too early.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: On the night before its eighth day, an animal may enter the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up רב פפא. A young animal may already become holy as מעשר on the night before its eighth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal cannot be offered until its eighth day. Yet it can become holy as מעשר בהמה the night before, which means that night is not treated as 'too early.' This is exactly רב פפא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל
The night before the eighth day
A pen for animals
To be tithed (to become מעשר בהמה)

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
On the night of the eighth day,
it enters the pen to be tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רב פפא's claim in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that night is not מחוסר זמן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל about tithing an animal on the night before its eighth day

steps.title: רבי אפטוריקי's contradiction between two parts of a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's view matches רבי אפטוריקי, who pointed out that one part of the פסוק implies the night before the eighth day is fit, and another part implies it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches רבי אפטוריקי, who pointed out a contradiction. It is written: 'It shall be seven days with its mother' — so the night after is fit. And it is written: 'From the eighth day and on it shall be accepted' — so that night is not fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second support, from רבי אפטוריקי. First it lays out his contradiction between two halves of a פסוק; the next step gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seven days with its mother' suggests that once seven days end, the following night is already fine. 'From the eighth day' suggests you must wait for the day itself. These two readings clash about the night before the eighth day.

keyTerms.meaning: He points out a contradiction between sources
Under (with) its mother
It shall be accepted (as an offering)
Is fit

phrases.english: And this is like Rabbi Appetoriki,
for Rabbi Appetoriki pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: "Then it shall be seven days under its mother";
so the night after is fit;
and it is written: "And from the eighth day and onward it shall be accepted";
so the night is not fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second support for רב פפא, starting with the contradiction that will be resolved in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that night is not מחוסר זמן

steps.title: Night for becoming holy, day for being offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אפטוריקי resolves the contradiction: on the night before the eighth day the animal may become holy, and on the eighth day it may be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we fit these together? The night is for becoming holy, and the day is for being accepted as an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אפטוריקי answers his own contradiction. Each half of the פסוק is talking about something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night before the eighth day is fit for making the animal holy, but offering it must wait for the day. This shows an animal can become holy the night before it may be offered and not be 'too early,' which is exactly what רב פפא needs for the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (How do we fit both together?)
Becoming holy (consecration)
Being accepted as an offering on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, an animal may be made holy the night before the day it can be offered, and it is not 'too early.' Night is for קדושה, day is for הרצאה.

phrases.english: How so?
The night is for becoming holy,
and the day is for being accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? לַיְלָה לִקְדוּשָּׁה, וְיוֹם לְהַרְצָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 16, completing the support for רב פפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each part of the פסוק refers to a different stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves of the פסוק disagree about whether the night before the eighth day is fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The night is fit for קדושה and the day for הרצאה, so becoming holy at night is not 'too early.'

steps.title: רבי זירא asks: Does רבי יוחנן hold living animals are pushed off forever?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי אבהו whether רבי יוחנן really holds that a living animal, once it cannot be offered, is permanently disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אבהו: Shall we say that רבי יוחנן holds that living animals can be pushed off forever?!
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבי זירא points out that the idea of a פסח being disqualified because it was set aside too early seems to rest on a big assumption about living animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion assumed that a פסח set aside when it could not yet be offered becomes unfit for good. That only works if living animals are נדחין, meaning once unfit they never become fit again. רבי זירא is surprised that רבי יוחנן would hold this.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (often a surprised suggestion)
He holds (this view)
Living animals
Permanently pushed off (disqualified for good)

steps.confusionAlert: נדחין does not just mean 'not fit right now.' It means the animal is pushed away forever, even after the problem goes away.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Abbahu:
Shall we say that Rabbi Yochanan holds
that living animals are pushed off for good?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: לֵימָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the רבי יוחנן and רבי אבהו discussion and questions the assumption underneath it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption, in רבי יוחנן's explanation as רבי אבהו understood it, that an animal set aside before it may be offered is disqualified forever
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Permanent disqualification only makes sense if living animals are נדחין, and it is surprising to say רבי יוחנן holds that.

steps.title: Yes: the case of the partners' animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו confirms that רבי יוחנן holds living animals are permanently pushed off, citing his ruling about an animal half-consecrated by one partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. As רבי יוחנן said: an animal owned by two partners, where one made his half holy, then bought the other half and made it holy too, is holy but may not be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers רבי זירא's question with a clear 'yes' and backs it up with a ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the first half was made holy, the animal could not be offered, because half of it still belonged to the partner. Even after the whole animal becomes holy, it stays unfit forever. This shows that once a living animal is pushed off, it cannot come back.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Partners who own something together
He made it holy (dedicated it to the בית המקדש)
It is holy
It is not offered on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Being holy and being fit to be offered are two different things. This animal is fully holy, but it still can never go on the מזבח.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes;
phrases.notes: רבי אבהו is answering רבי זירא's question from the step before.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
An animal belonging to two partners –
if one consecrated his half of it,
and then bought the other half and consecrated it –
it is holy, but it is not offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין; דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוחנן hold that a living animal that becomes unfit is pushed off forever?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, as shown by his ruling that a partnership animal consecrated half by half is holy but never offered.

steps.title: The partners' animal can still make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's ruling continues: this animal can create a תמורה, and the substitute has the same status as the original.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it makes a substitute, and its substitute is like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting רבי יוחנן's ruling, adding what happens if someone tries to swap this animal for another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the animal is truly holy, swapping a regular animal for it makes the new animal holy too (תמורה). But the new animal copies the original's status: holy, yet never offered.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: a regular animal swapped for a holy one, which then becomes holy too
Just like it, with the same status

phrases.english: And it makes a substitute,
phrases.notes: If the owner swaps a regular animal for this one, the regular animal becomes holy.

phrases.english: and its substitute is like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ruling of רבי יוחנן quoted in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The partnership animal can create a תמורה, and the תמורה is holy but cannot be offered, just like the original.

steps.title: Three lessons from רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins listing three lessons learned from the ruling: living animals can be pushed off, and something unfit from the start counts as pushed off. The third lesson continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it three things: learn from it that living animals are pushed off; and learn from it that something pushed off from the start is pushed off; and learn from it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls general rules out of רבי יוחנן's case. It lists two of them here, and the third continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lesson one: a living animal can be permanently disqualified, which answers רבי זירא's question. Lesson two: even if the animal was unfit from the very moment it became holy, not unfit later on, it is still considered pushed off forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: we can conclude from this
Three
Living animals can be permanently pushed off
Pushed off from the start, unfit from the moment it became holy

steps.whatToRemember: From the partners' animal we learn that living animals can be pushed off forever, even when they were unfit from the very beginning.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two rules answer רבי זירא's question and settle רבי יוחנן's view on pushed-off animals.

phrases.english: And learn from it three things:
learn from it that living animals are pushed off,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דָּחוּי מֵעִיקָּרָא הָוֵה דָּחוּי,
phrases.english: and learn from it that something pushed off from the start is pushed off,
and learn from it...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws general conclusions from רבי יוחנן's ruling quoted in steps 19-20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Living animals can be permanently pushed off, and disqualification from the very start counts as being pushed off. The third lesson follows in the next section.
